question:
A customer reports a defect in the executable we shipped to them two years ago, and to investigate it we need that very same executable back, byte for byte, but the toolchain and third-party libraries on our machines have been upgraded since then. What should the team have been tracking and preserving so that this would be possible?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

To reproduce a shipped executable byte-for-byte after toolchain upgrades, teams must place all software configuration items—source code, compilers, build scripts, third-party libraries, and related artifacts—under SCM control, track baselines, and preserve build instructions and tool versions so previous releases can be reliably reconstructed.

# Guidelines

- Place supporting tools (e.g., compilers) and build instructions under SCM control so the correct versions are available [SWEBOK excerpt b4b4c90248f42cd3ae78] software configuration item. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt e082f1c815b2042b56a6]")

- Ensure SCM can [SWEBOK excerpt af43ae3c37d081b1c9b8], since [SWEBOK excerpt 3b956e0bfb310bd75635]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/In-Process Audits and Software Release Management.md)

- Identify and control all software items with potential to become SCIs, including plans, specifications, [SWEBOK excerpt 734701d9bbc5afb70595] documentation. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management and Change Control/Software Configuration Items Selection and Change Recording.md)

- Use a repository to store binaries created during the build process so that the latest build artifacts can be extracted and redeployed as required during release verification. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Configuration Management System Tools and Components.md)

- Track version control of source code, configuration files, and related artifacts throughout the project lifecycle. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Configuration Management System Tools and Components.md)

- Document the physical contents of each release in a version description document (VDD), and select the correct variants of product items given the product's intended application. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Software Release Management and Deployment Processes.md)

- Maintain an SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) listing the artifacts included in each build as an important CM output. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Build Quality Assurance and Configuration Management/Software Build Artifacts and Continuous Integration Processes.md)

- Preserve build process outputs for future reference, as [SWEBOK excerpt add63e8c4716ff08c1cf]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Build Quality Assurance and Configuration Management/Build Process Quality Verification and Documentation.md)

- Plan SCM for [SWEBOK excerpt b193be691c4244a432a8], managing them with configuration control and tracking how changes or updates are evaluated and managed. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Interface Control/SCM Workbenches and Vendor Control Planning.md)

- Establish baselines at points where stability is intended, and control all changes including variants, so the exact configuration of any prior release can be identified and reconstructed. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Configuration Management and Change Control/Baselines and Change Management in Configuration Control.md)
